items.prompt: Mia has 12 stickers. Ben has 7 more than Mia. How many stickers do they have together?

figure.alt: A bar model. Mia has a bar of 12. Ben has a bar of 12 and a short extra part of 7.

hints: Find how many stickers Ben has.
Ben has 12 and 7 more.
Add Mia's stickers and Ben's stickers.
items.explanation: Ben has 12 + 7 = 19 stickers. Together they have 12 + 19 = 31 stickers.

items.prompt: Red marbles are 3 times as many as blue marbles. There are 24 marbles in all. How many blue marbles are there?

figure.alt: A bar model. Blue is one block. Red is three blocks of the same size.

hints: Draw one block for the blue marbles.
The red marbles are 3 blocks. How many blocks in all?
Share 24 between all the blocks.
items.explanation: Blue is 1 block and red is 3 blocks. That makes 4 blocks in all. 24 / 4 = 6, so there are 6 blue marbles.

solution.say: Blue is 1 block and red is 3 blocks.

items.prompt: Ani and Bela have 30 stickers together. Ani has 6 more stickers than Bela. How many stickers does Ani have?

figure.alt: A bar model. Ani has a bar the same as Bela, plus an extra part of 6. Together they have 30.

hints: Take away the extra 6 stickers first.
Then Ani and Bela would have the same.
Share what is left equally.
items.explanation: Take away the extra 6: 30 - 6 = 24. Share equally: 24 / 2 = 12 for Bela. Ani has 12 + 6 = 18 stickers.

items.prompt: A rope is 20 m long. It is cut into 2 pieces. One piece is 4 m longer than the other. How long is the longer piece, in metres?
hints: Take away the extra 4 m.
16 m is left. Share it between the two pieces.
The shorter piece is 8 m. How long is the longer one?
items.explanation: Take away the extra 4 m: 20 - 4 = 16. Each piece would be 8 m. The longer piece is 8 + 4 = 12 m.

items.prompt: Sam has 5 times as many cards as Tia. Together they have 18 cards. How many cards does Tia have?
hints: Draw one block for Tia.
Sam has 5 blocks. How many blocks together?
Share 18 between the blocks.
items.explanation: Tia has 1 block and Sam has 5 blocks. That is 6 blocks in all. 18 / 6 = 3, so Tia has 3 cards.

solution.say: Tia has 1 block and Sam has 5 blocks.

items.prompt: Three boxes hold 37 balls in all. Box B has 4 more balls than box A. Box C has 2 more balls than box B. How many balls are in box A?
hints: Take away the extras to make the boxes equal.
Box B has 4 extra. Box C has 4 + 2 = 6 extra.
Take away 4 and 6 from 37, then share between 3 boxes.
items.explanation: Box B has 4 extra and box C has 6 extra, so 10 extra in all. 37 - 10 = 27. Share between 3 boxes: 27 / 3 = 9. Box A has 9 balls.

solution.say: Box B has 4 extra and box C has 6 extra, so 10 extra in all.

items.prompt: Dina read half of her book. She has 15 pages left to read. How many pages does the book have?
hints: Half of the book is already read.
The other half is 15 pages.
Double 15.
items.explanation: The 15 pages left are the other half of the book. The whole book is 15 + 15 = 30 pages.

solution.say: The 15 pages left are the other half of the book.

items.prompt: A class has 28 children. There are 4 more girls than boys. How many boys are there?
hints: Take away the 4 extra girls.
Then there are the same number of boys and girls.
Share the rest equally.
items.explanation: Take away the 4 extra girls: 28 - 4 = 24. Share equally: 24 / 2 = 12 boys. There are 16 girls.

items.prompt: Tom has 3 times as many cards as Jo. Tom gives 8 cards to Jo. Now they have the same number of cards. How many cards did Tom have at the start?
hints: After the gift, they have the same number.
Tom had 3 blocks. After he gives 8, he has 3 blocks - 8.
Jo had 1 block. After the gift, Jo has 1 block + 8.
items.explanation: Tom had 3 blocks and Jo had 1 block. After the gift, 3 blocks - 8 = 1 block + 8. So 2 blocks = 16, which means 1 block = 8. Tom started with 3 x 8 = 24 cards.

solution.say: Tom had 3 blocks and Jo had 1 block.

items.prompt: Two numbers add up to 30. One number is 6 more than the other. What is the smaller number?
hints: Take away the extra 6.
Share the rest equally.
items.explanation: Take away the 6: 30 - 6 = 24. Share equally: 24 / 2 = 12. The smaller number is 12 and the bigger is 18.

solution.say: The smaller number is 12 and the bigger is 18.

items.prompt: 3 bags each hold the same number of oranges. There are also 5 loose oranges. In all there are 29 oranges. How many oranges are in each bag?
hints: Take away the loose oranges first.
Share 24 between the 3 bags.
items.explanation: Take away the 5 loose oranges: 29 - 5 = 24. Share between 3 bags: 24 / 3 = 8. Each bag holds 8 oranges.

items.prompt: Amy has twice as many stickers as Bo. Cy has 5 fewer stickers than Amy. Together they have 25 stickers. How many stickers does Bo have?
hints: Draw one block for Bo.
Amy has 2 blocks. Cy has 2 blocks and then 5 less.
Add the blocks and the missing 5.
items.explanation: Bo has 1 block, Amy 2 blocks and Cy 2 blocks - 5. In all there are 5 blocks - 5 = 25. So 5 blocks = 30 and 1 block = 6. Bo has 6 stickers.

solution.say: Bo has 1 block, Amy 2 blocks and Cy 2 blocks - 5.

items.prompt: A rod is 36 cm long. The red part is 2 times as long as the blue part. How long is the red part, in cm?
hints: The blue part is 1 block.
The red part is 2 blocks. How many blocks in all?
Share 36 between 3 blocks.
items.explanation: The blue part is 1 block and the red part is 2 blocks. That is 3 blocks in all. 36 / 3 = 12 cm for the blue part. The red part is 2 x 12 = 24 cm.

solution.say: The blue part is 1 block and the red part is 2 blocks.
The red part is 2 x 12 = 24 cm.

items.prompt: A farm has 29 cows and hens. There are 5 more cows than hens. How many cows are there?
hints: Take away the 5 extra cows.
Then there are the same number of cows and hens.
Share the rest equally to find the hens.
items.explanation: Take away the 5 extra cows: 29 - 5 = 24. Share equally: 24 / 2 = 12 hens. There are 12 + 5 = 17 cows.

items.prompt: The top shelf has 28 books. The bottom shelf has 18 books. How many books must move down to make the shelves equal?
hints: Find how many more books the top shelf has.
The top shelf has 10 more.
Moving a book changes the difference by 2.
items.explanation: The top shelf has 28 - 18 = 10 more books. Each book that moves makes the gap 2 smaller. So 10 / 2 = 5 books must move.

solution.say: The top shelf has 28 - 18 = 10 more books.
Each book that moves makes the gap 2 smaller.

items.prompt: Rod A is 7 cm longer than rod B. Rod B is 4 cm longer than rod C. Rods A and C together are 25 cm long. How long is rod B, in cm?
hints: Compare A and C. How much longer is A than C?
A is 7 + 4 = 11 cm longer than C.
Take away the extra 11 cm from 25 cm.
items.explanation: A is 11 cm longer than C. Take away the extra: 25 - 11 = 14. Share equally: C is 7 cm. Then B is 7 + 4 = 11 cm, and A is 18 cm.

solution.say: A is 11 cm longer than C.
Then B is 7 + 4 = 11 cm, and A is 18 cm.

items.prompt: A tank is half full. It has 18 litres of water in it. How many more litres fill the tank?
hints: Half of the tank is full.
The other half is empty.
How much water is in the full half?
items.explanation: The tank is half full with 18 litres. The empty half also holds 18 litres. So 18 more litres fill the tank.

solution.say: The tank is half full with 18 litres.
The empty half also holds 18 litres.
So 18 more litres fill the tank.

items.prompt: There are 14 children in the park. 5 more children come. Then 8 go home. How many children are in the park now?
hints: Do it in the order of the story.
14 and 5 more.
Then take away the 8 who go home.
items.explanation: 14 + 5 = 19 children. Then 19 - 8 = 11 children are in the park.

solution.say: Then 19 - 8 = 11 children are in the park.

items.prompt: A box holds 6 eggs. Mum buys 5 boxes and uses 13 eggs. How many eggs are left?
hints: Find how many eggs there are in 5 boxes.
5 boxes of 6 eggs.
Take away the eggs she uses.
items.explanation: 5 boxes hold 5 x 6 = 30 eggs. Mum uses 13, so 30 - 13 = 17 eggs are left.

solution.say: Mum uses 13, so 30 - 13 = 17 eggs are left.

items.prompt: Ben has 36 sweets. He keeps 8. He gives the same number to each of 4 friends. How many sweets does each friend get?
hints: Find how many sweets Ben gives away.
Share the 28 between the 4 friends.
items.explanation: Ben gives away 36 - 8 = 28 sweets. Each friend gets 28 / 4 = 7 sweets.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I add 7 and get 15. What is my number?
hints: Undo the adding.
The opposite of adding 7 is taking away 7.
Take 7 away from 15.
items.explanation: The opposite of adding 7 is taking away 7. 15 - 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15.

solution.say: The opposite of adding 7 is taking away 7.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I double it and take away 3. The answer is 11. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards. Undo the last step first.
The last step was take away 3. Undo it: add 3.
Then undo the doubling.
items.explanation: Undo take away 3 by adding 3: 11 + 3 = 14. Undo doubling by halving: 14 / 2 = 7. Check: 7 x 2 = 14 and 14 - 3 = 11.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I take away 6 and then double the answer. I get 20. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards. Undo the last step first.
The last step was doubling. Undo it by halving.
Then undo the take away 6.
items.explanation: Undo doubling by halving: 20 / 2 = 10. Undo take away 6 by adding 6: 10 + 6 = 16. Check: 16 - 6 = 10 and 10 x 2 = 20.

items.prompt: Dewi had some stickers. She gave 5 to Ana. Bo gave her 3 more. Now she has 12 stickers. How many stickers did she have at the start?
hints: Work backwards from 12.
The last thing that happened was Bo gave her 3. Undo it.
Then undo the 5 she gave to Ana.
items.explanation: Before Bo gave her 3 she had 12 - 3 = 9. Before she gave 5 to Ana she had 9 + 5 = 14 stickers.

solution.say: Before Bo gave her 3 she had 12 - 3 = 9.
Before she gave 5 to Ana she had 9 + 5 = 14 stickers.

items.prompt: Mia spent half of her money on a book. Then she spent Rp1.000 on a pen. She has Rp2.000 left. How many rupiah did Mia have at the start?
hints: Work backwards from what is left.
Before the pen she had Rp2.000 + Rp1.000.
That was what was left after the book. Undo the half.
items.explanation: Before buying the pen she had Rp2.000 + Rp1.000 = Rp3.000. That was half of her money. So she started with Rp3.000 x 2 = Rp6.000.

solution.say: Before buying the pen she had Rp2.000 + Rp1.000 = Rp3.000.
That was half of her money.
So she started with Rp3.000 x 2 = Rp6.000.

items.prompt: Sam ate half of the cookies. Then he ate 2 more. Now 3 cookies are left. How many cookies were there at the start?
hints: Work backwards from 3.
Before he ate 2 more there were 3 + 2.
That was half of the cookies.
items.explanation: Before he ate 2 more there were 3 + 2 = 5 cookies. That was half of the cookies, so there were 5 x 2 = 10 at the start.

solution.say: Before he ate 2 more there were 3 + 2 = 5 cookies.
That was half of the cookies, so there were 5 x 2 = 10 at the start.

items.prompt: At a bus stop, 5 people get off. Then 8 people get on. Now there are 20 people on the bus. How many people were on the bus before the stop?
hints: Work backwards from 20.
Undo the 8 who got on. Then undo the 5 who got off.
20 - 8 = 12. Then add the 5 back.
items.explanation: Before the 8 got on, there were 20 - 8 = 12. Before the 5 got off, there were 12 + 5 = 17 people.

solution.say: Before the 8 got on, there were 20 - 8 = 12.
Before the 5 got off, there were 12 + 5 = 17 people.

items.prompt: A machine multiplies a number by 3 and then takes away 4. The answer is 17. What number went in?
hints: Work backwards from 17.
Undo the take away 4 by adding 4.
Then undo the times 3.
items.explanation: Undo take away 4: 17 + 4 = 21. Undo times 3: 21 / 3 = 7. Check: 7 x 3 = 21 and 21 - 4 = 17.

items.prompt: A pond loses half of its water every day. After 3 days it has 5 litres. How many litres did it have at the start?
hints: Work backwards from 5.
Each day the water is halved. Undo it by doubling.
Double three times.
items.explanation: Doubling back for each of the 3 days: 5 x 2 = 10, then 20, then 40. The pond started with 40 litres.

solution.say: Doubling back for each of the 3 days: 5 x 2 = 10, then 20, then 40.

items.prompt: In 5 years Raka will be 12. How old is Raka now?
hints: Work backwards. Go back 5 years.
Take 5 away from 12.
items.explanation: In 5 years he will be 12, so now he is 12 - 5 = 7 years old.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I add 3, double it, then take away 4. The answer is 14. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards from 14.
Undo take away 4. Then undo the doubling.
Last, undo the add 3.
items.explanation: Undo take away 4: 14 + 4 = 18. Undo doubling: 18 / 2 = 9. Undo add 3: 9 - 3 = 6. Check: 6 + 3 = 9, 9 x 2 = 18 and 18 - 4 = 14.

items.prompt: A shop had 50 apples. It sold some in the morning and 12 in the afternoon. 9 apples are left. How many apples did it sell in the morning?
hints: Find how many apples were sold in all.
50 - 9 = 41 apples were sold in all.
Take away the 12 sold in the afternoon.
items.explanation: The shop sold 50 - 9 = 41 apples in all. It sold 12 in the afternoon, so 41 - 12 = 29 in the morning.

solution.say: The shop sold 50 - 9 = 41 apples in all.
It sold 12 in the afternoon, so 41 - 12 = 29 in the morning.

items.prompt: Each time Ana gives away half of her sweets and 1 more. She does this twice. Then she has 2 sweets left. How many sweets did she have at the start?
hints: Work backwards from 2.
Before the last gift she gave 1 more and half. Undo: 2 + 1, then double.
Do this once more for the first gift.
items.explanation: Before the second gift she had (2 + 1) x 2 = 6. Before the first gift she had (6 + 1) x 2 = 14. Check: 14 gives 7 + 1 = 8 and keeps 6. Then 6 gives 3 + 1 = 4 and keeps 2.

solution.say: Before the second gift she had (2 + 1) x 2 = 6.
Before the first gift she had (6 + 1) x 2 = 14.

items.prompt: School ends at 12:15. There were two 45 minute lessons and a 30 minute break. School began at the start of the first lesson. When did school begin?

options.why: The lessons and the break take 2 hours in all.
Count only the 2 lessons and the break.

hints: Find the time school took in all.
45 + 45 + 30 minutes.
Count back from 12:15.
items.explanation: The lessons and the break take 45 + 45 + 30 = 120 minutes, which is 2 hours. 2 hours before 12:15 is 10:15.

solution.say: The lessons and the break take 45 + 45 + 30 = 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I add 9 and then take away 4. The answer is 30. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards from 30.
Undo take away 4. Then undo add 9.
30 + 4, then take away 9.
items.explanation: Undo take away 4: 30 + 4 = 34. Undo add 9: 34 - 9 = 25. Check: 25 + 9 = 34 and 34 - 4 = 30.

items.prompt: Ali is 7 years old. His sister is 3 years older. How old will his sister be in 4 years?
hints: Find how old his sister is now.
She is 7 + 3 now.
Then add the 4 years.
items.explanation: His sister is 7 + 3 = 10 years old now. In 4 years she will be 10 + 4 = 14.

solution.say: His sister is 7 + 3 = 10 years old now.

items.prompt: Mum is 4 times as old as Dina. Dina is 8 years old. How old will Mum be when Dina is 12?
hints: Find how old Mum is now.
Mum is 4 x 8.
Dina needs 4 more years to be 12.
items.explanation: Mum is 4 x 8 = 32 now. Dina will be 12 in 4 years, so Mum will be 32 + 4 = 36.

solution.say: Dina will be 12 in 4 years, so Mum will be 32 + 4 = 36.

items.prompt: In 6 years Rani will be 10. How old was Rani 3 years ago?
hints: Find how old Rani is now.
In 6 years she will be 10, so now she is 10 - 6.
Then go back 3 years.
items.explanation: Rani is 10 - 6 = 4 now. Three years ago she was 4 - 3 = 1 year old.

solution.say: Three years ago she was 4 - 3 = 1 year old.

items.prompt: A father is 30 years older than his son. Together they are 38 years old. How old is the father?
hints: Take away the 30 extra years.
Share 8 equally to find the son's age.
items.explanation: Take away the extra 30: 38 - 30 = 8. The son is 8 / 2 = 4. The father is 4 + 30 = 34.

items.prompt: Two sisters are 5 and 9 years old. In how many years will their ages add up to 24?
hints: Add their ages now.
They add up to 14 now.
Each year both sisters get 1 year older. How much does the total go up?
items.explanation: Their ages add up to 14 now. Each year the total goes up by 2. They need 24 - 14 = 10 more, so it takes 10 / 2 = 5 years.

solution.say: Their ages add up to 14 now.
Each year the total goes up by 2.
They need 24 - 14 = 10 more, so it takes 10 / 2 = 5 years.

items.prompt: Ben is 3 years older than Ani. Ani is 2 years older than Cat. Cat is 6. How old is Ben?
hints: Find Ani's age first.
Ani is 2 years older than Cat.
Then add 3 for Ben.
items.explanation: Ani is 6 + 2 = 8. Ben is 8 + 3 = 11 years old.

items.prompt: Mia is 6 and her brother is 10. How old will her brother be when Mia is 10?
hints: The age gap between them stays the same.
The gap is 10 - 6 = 4 years.
Add the gap to Mia's age.
items.explanation: The gap between their ages is always 4 years. When Mia is 10, her brother is 10 + 4 = 14.

solution.say: The gap between their ages is always 4 years.
When Mia is 10, her brother is 10 + 4 = 14.

items.prompt: A 2-digit number has a tens digit twice its ones digit. The digits add up to 9. What is the number?
hints: The ones digit is 1 block. The tens digit is 2 blocks.
The digits add up to 3 blocks.
3 blocks make 9.
items.explanation: The tens digit is 2 blocks and the ones digit is 1 block. 3 blocks make 9, so 1 block is 3. The tens digit is 6, and the number is 63.

solution.say: The tens digit is 2 blocks and the ones digit is 1 block.
The tens digit is 6, and the number is 63.

items.prompt: Three numbers in a row add up to 24. What is the smallest of the three numbers?
hints: The middle number is the average of the three.
The smallest is 1 less than the middle number.
items.explanation: The middle number is 24 / 3 = 8. The numbers are 7, 8 and 9. The smallest number is 7.

items.prompt: Four numbers in a row add up to 34. What is the smallest of the four numbers?
hints: The numbers go up by 1 each time.
Guess a starting number and add the four numbers.
If the total is too low, start with a bigger number.
items.explanation: Try 7, 8, 9, 10. They add up to 7 + 8 + 9 + 10 = 34. So the smallest number is 7.

items.prompt: Take two neighbours in the list 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on. They add up to 24. What is the bigger number?
hints: Odd numbers go up by 2 each time.
Half of 24 is 12.
One number is just below 12 and one is just above.
items.explanation: The numbers are on each side of 12 and differ by 2, so they are 11 and 13. 11 + 13 = 24. The bigger number is 13.

solution.say: The numbers are on each side of 12 and differ by 2, so they are 11 and 13.

items.prompt: I double a number and add 5. This gives the same answer as adding 12 to the number. What is my number?
hints: Try a number and see which side is bigger.
Doubling and adding 5 is 5 more than the number, plus the number again.
The number itself must make up the gap of 7.
items.explanation: Doubling and adding 5 means number + number + 5. Adding 12 means number + 12. Take away the number from both: number + 5 = 12. So the number is 7. Check: 7 x 2 + 5 = 19 and 7 + 12 = 19.

solution.say: Doubling and adding 5 means number + number + 5.
Take away the number from both: number + 5 = 12.

items.prompt: How many more than 17 is double 12?
hints: Find double 12 first.
Double 12 is 24.
Take 17 away from it.
items.explanation: Double 12 is 24. 24 - 17 = 7. So double 12 is 7 more than 17.

items.prompt: Half of a number is 14. What is a quarter of the number?
hints: Find the number first.
Half of the number is 14, so the number is 28.
A quarter is half of a half.
items.explanation: The number is 14 x 2 = 28. A quarter of 28 is 7. Also, a quarter is half of 14, which is 7.

solution.say: Also, a quarter is half of 14, which is 7.

items.prompt: Two numbers multiply to 12 and add up to 7. What is the bigger number?
hints: List pairs of numbers that multiply to 12.
They are 1 and 12, 2 and 6, and 3 and 4.
Which pair adds up to 7?
items.explanation: The pairs that multiply to 12 are 1 and 12, 2 and 6, and 3 and 4. Only 3 + 4 = 7. The bigger number is 4.

solution.say: The pairs that multiply to 12 are 1 and 12, 2 and 6, and 3 and 4.
